chapters.title: Opening
chapters.text: Once upon a shot, Erdem had one important talk to give, and seven things to remember. So Erdem built a palace in the mind, and walked it, one room at a time.

chapters.title: PLAN
chapters.text: Station one. Entrance Courtyard. A giant golden compass draws the shot on the floor. Erdem starts with the question every director asks: who is the hero, what is the setting, what is the move, and what is the look.

chapters.title: SETTING
chapters.text: Station two. Colonnade. Forty white columns hold up a mountain, a city, a tree and a wave. Erdem builds the set in plain grey shapes, at real size, so nothing surprises them later.

chapters.title: MOVE
chapters.text: Station three. Rotunda. A red arrow circles the marble ring. Erdem chooses one camera move with care: a dolly, an orbit, a chase, a crane or a truck.

chapters.title: CLAY
chapters.text: Station four. Sunken Garden. Giant clay figures sculpt the world in grey. No colour yet. The shape has to carry the story alone.

chapters.title: CHECK
chapters.text: Station five. Library Bridge. Three numbers glow in the air: frame one, frame one hundred and twenty, frame two hundred and forty. Erdem looks through the camera, fixes what is wrong, and looks again.

chapters.title: PROMPT
chapters.text: Station six. Observatory. A glass sphere projects words into the night sky. Lock the camera first, then describe the look, in two to four sentences.

chapters.title: RENDER
chapters.text: Station seven. Summit Altar. A flame launches the film into the sky. Ten seconds, rendered and ready. Erdem remembers all seven, in order, and walks back down the stairs knowing the way.

chapters.title: Closing
chapters.text: And you, watching this, Erdem: pick your own seven things, and build your own palace. The route is yours, and so is the memory.
